steps.stem: An economist said: "Whether the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures will be sustained remains highly uncertain, particularly in light of the other developments in the market; what we are seeing is, so far, no more than an early indication." Which of the following sentences expresses the same meaning as the economist's statement?
choices: If we take into account the other developments in the market, it is certain that the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures will continue
It is uncertain whether the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures accurately reflects the current state of the market
Last quarter's sales figures are admittedly no more than an early indication, but it is already clear that the recovery they suggest will be sustained
Given the other developments in the market, it is doubtful whether the recovery suggested by last quarter's sales figures will last for long
explanation: The economist doubts whether the recovery will last, because of other developments in the market. (1) and (3) turn the doubt into certainty; (2) moves the doubt from the future to the present.

steps.stem: Maya: "At the new restaurant on Elm Street, most diners come back, so I assume the food there is ____." Maya's words are not logical, but they would have been logical had she said ____ instead of "so," ____ instead of ____. Which of the following best completes the text?
choices: disappointing / "therefore" / or "few diners fail to come back" / "most diners come back"
excellent / "even so" / or alternatively "not excellent" / "excellent"
disappointing / "even so" / or "excellent" / "disappointing"
mediocre / "and yet" / and also "quite good" / "mediocre"
explanation: "Most come back, so … disappointing" is illogical; it becomes logical with a concession ("even so") or with a verdict that fits the evidence ("excellent"). (1) swaps in a synonym and a paraphrase, which change nothing; (2) starts from a logical sentence; (4) requires both changes at once, which makes the sentence illogical again.

steps.stem: The following sentence, taken from an announcement about a scholarship, can be understood in two ways: "The scholarship will be awarded only to nursing students who work at the city hospital and residents of the northern district." Which of the following is not possible according to either of the two ways of understanding the sentence?
choices: Yael, who works at the city hospital but is not a nursing student and does not live in the northern district, was awarded the scholarship
Ron, a resident of the northern district who is not a nursing student and does not work at the city hospital, was awarded the scholarship
Shira, a nursing student who lives in the northern district but does not work at the city hospital, was awarded the scholarship
Gil, a resident of the northern district who is not a nursing student and does not work at the city hospital, was not awarded the scholarship
explanation: Reading 1: nursing student + hospital + north; reading 2: (nursing student + hospital) or a resident of the north. Yael is not a nursing student and does not live in the north, so she fails both. Ron and Shira fit reading 2, and "only" never forces an award, so Gil is always possible.

steps.stem: A researcher examined the effect of room temperature on willingness to donate. One group of participants waited for a quarter of an hour in a warm room, and another group in a cool room. Then all the participants were asked to contribute to a fund for renovating a local playground. Those who had waited in the warm room donated considerably more, and the researcher estimated that, since warmth improves mood, these participants had been in a better mood when asked to donate. Which of the following assumptions underlies the researcher's estimate?
choices: A person in a bad mood does not notice the room's temperature, so it makes no difference to them whether the room is warm or cool
A person in a good mood contributes more generously to a cause than a person whose mood is less good
Waiting in a warm room causes people to support playground renovation more than people who waited in a cool room
A good mood causes a person to donate more generously, provided that they have spent time in a warm room beforehand
explanation: The estimate runs warmth → good mood → larger donations; the researcher must assume the second link. (4) adds a condition the estimate does not need; (1) is irrelevant and (3) merely restates the finding.

steps.stem: Noa: "I doubt that I could arrange this violin sonata for the piano, much less for the guitar." Eyal: "What you say implies that you play the piano better than you play the guitar." Eyal's claim is based on the assumption that a musician who finds it easier to arrange a piece ____ plays instrument A better than instrument B.
choices: from instrument A for instrument C than from instrument A for instrument B
from instrument A for instrument C than from instrument B for instrument C
from instrument A for instrument B than from instrument B for instrument A
from instrument C for instrument A than from instrument C for instrument B
explanation: Noa finds violin → piano easier than violin → guitar, and Eyal concludes that she plays the piano better, so ease of arranging for an instrument must reflect command of it: from C (violin) for A (piano) rather than for B (guitar). The other choices put the instruments in the wrong roles.

steps.title: Understanding sentences - the toolkit
steps.intro: What makes a sentence hard, and what to do about it.

head: Difficulty
What to do
rows: Eliminate by structure first; the key expression decides the rest
Find what makes it (il)logical; test each swap
Turn one pair of negatives into a positive at a time
Write both readings ("and" can act as "or"); check each choice against both
Find the unstated link between what was said and the conclusion

tips: "Only" = who can be accepted - not who must be.
The skill runs through all of verbal: no understanding, no conclusions.

steps.stem: A clipping is a word formed by cutting off part of a longer word while keeping its meaning: "exam," for instance, was formed from "examination" and means exactly the same thing. Clippings are common in everyday speech, and many speakers are not even aware that the short form was once part of a longer word. Clippings are of two kinds. In a back clipping, the end of the longer word is removed and its beginning is kept: "lab" from "laboratory," for example. In a fore clipping, the beginning of the longer word is removed and its end is kept: "phone" from "telephone," for example. Thus "bus," formed from "omnibus," is a ____ clipping, whereas "memo," formed from "memorandum," is a ____ clipping. Which of the following completes the sentence correctly?
choices: back / back
back / fore
fore / back
fore / fore
explanation: "Bus" keeps the end of "omnibus" (fore clipping); "memo" keeps the beginning of "memorandum" (back clipping). The trap is to mix up the part that is removed with the part that is kept.

steps.stem: In an interview about her new cookbook, a well-known chef was asked what makes a dish good, and answered: "Season it as boldly as you like - but never so boldly that the ingredients disappear." Which of the following sentences best expresses the chef's intention?
choices: Every good dish should be seasoned boldly enough to satisfy diners who like strong flavors
Although bold seasoning is a virtue in cooking, too much of it hides the very ingredients the dish is meant to present
A good dish is built on the boldest and most basic of its ingredients
The boldness of the seasoning matters no less than the quality of the ingredients
explanation: The second half of the answer sets a limit on the first: season boldly, but not past the point where the ingredients are lost. (1) drops the limit; (3) turns advice about seasoning into advice about choosing ingredients; (4) makes the two equal instead of one limiting the other.

steps.stem: At the entrance to the Morvin Concert Hall hangs a plaque quoting the conductor Ada Morvin, from a radio interview she gave in 1984: "I built this orchestra with my own hands." Many of her former musicians protested, arguing that the sentence from which the quotation was taken reflected her well-known humility, whereas the quotation on its own made her sound arrogant - the very opposite of who she was. Which of the following sentences is most likely to be the one from which the quotation was taken?
choices: "The only sense in which I built this orchestra with my own hands is that I set out the chairs before every rehearsal"
"I built this orchestra with my own hands, and I will always miss the years we spent together"
"It cost me my health and most of my savings, but I built this orchestra with my own hands"
"I built this orchestra with my own hands, and the concert hall and the music school as well"
explanation: Only (1) turns the words into modest self-mockery, which the quotation on its own erases. (2) adds longing, (3) sacrifice and (4) scope; none reverses the boast, and (3) and (4) even strengthen it.

steps.stem: Ofra invented a new word - "mazlit." To show her brother what it means, she said: "This year mazlit the apricots on our tree ripened in the same week, so we had to make jam for three days straight." In which of the following sentences does "mazlit" appear with the same meaning it has in Ofra's sentence?
choices: Because mazlit the students passed the final exam, the teacher decided to go over the whole course again
The curve is considered dangerous because mazlit the drivers who reach it slow down in time
After the storm, mazlit the windows in the old school were broken, so the classes were moved to the new building
Since mazlit the town's residents own a car, the bus service is used by almost everyone
explanation: Ofra's consequence fixes "mazlit" as "nearly all"; only in (3) does the consequence fit nearly all the windows being broken. In (1), (2) and (4) the consequences require "only a few."

steps.stem: A team of zoologists had long assumed that the ability to tell individual voices apart exists only in human beings, in the apes and in horses. A recent study of theirs, however, found that a certain species of tree frog also has this ability - a finding that puzzled them, since frogs are only very distantly related to human beings, and the frog's hearing organ is simple. The researchers suggest that the ability developed in the frogs independently, because they breed in dense choruses in which telling one caller from another is important. Which of the following claims is not implied by the paragraph?
choices: It has long been assumed that the ability to tell voices apart requires a complex hearing organ
It has long been assumed that the apes' ability to tell voices apart is connected with their close evolutionary relationship to human beings
The researchers hold that the ability to tell voices apart may also develop in other animals that breed in dense groups
The researchers hold that the ability to tell voices apart exists in many animals that are only distantly related to human beings
explanation: The paragraph reports a single such species, not many. The zoologists' puzzlement implies the assumptions in (1) (the frog's simple hearing organ) and (2) (its distant relationship to human beings), and the researchers' reason implies (3).

steps.stem: The following sentence can be understood in several different ways: "The campaign of the former party's spokesman with the students' union has ended." Which of the following is not one of the ways of understanding the sentence?
choices: The campaign that the spokesman of a party that no longer exists waged against the students' union has ended
The campaign that the spokesman waged against the former party of the students' union has ended
The campaign that the party's ex-spokesman waged against the students' union has ended
The campaign that the former party's spokesman waged, together with the students' union, against another body has ended
explanation: "Former" can describe the party or the spokesman, and "with" can mean "against" or "together with"; (1), (3) and (4) follow these options. (2) makes the party belong to the students' union, which no reading allows.

steps.stem: At the end of the season, the conductor of a youth choir said to the singers: "Every one of you has improved this year - though a little more than a third of you have improved less than I had hoped." How many of the singers have improved less than the conductor had hoped?
choices: A little more than a third of them
A little fewer than two thirds of them
Many more than a third of them
Many fewer than a third of them
explanation: The conductor says so directly. The traps are to read "every one of you has improved" as praise that cancels the reservation, or to count the other group (a little fewer than two thirds).

steps.stem: A lecturer in management wished to illustrate a claim to her students, and said: "If one door on the street sticks, call the carpenter; if every door on the street sticks, look at the weather." Which of the following claims is the one the lecturer wished to illustrate?
choices: A manager should deal with an organization's minor problems before turning to its major ones
A problem that appears in only one department is usually more serious than a problem that appears in all of them
Managers should not assume that a problem that is common today will remain common in the future
When the same problem appears in every department of an organization, its cause should be sought in something they all share, and not in each department separately
explanation: One sticking door points to a local fault; all of them sticking points to a shared cause. The other claims may be sound advice, but the image says nothing about them.

choices: Typing "a dog barked" as "a dig barked"
Typing "a new form" as "a new from"
Typing "a long letter" as "a long leter"
Typing "a black cat" as "a black caat"
explanation: (1) strikes a neighboring key, (3) drops one of the double t's and (4) types a letter twice. (2) swaps two letters, which is none of the three.

steps.stem: The word "apron" names a garment worn over the front of one's clothes. Linguists explain, however, that the older form of the word was "napron": the form "apron" arose because speakers heard "a napron" as "an apron" and took the "n" to belong to the word before it. Linguists point out that the same thing happened to the word "adder," which developed in the same way from "nadder." Which of the following words could replace "adder" in the linguists' example?
choices: "newt" (from the older "ewt")
"oven"
"apple"
"umpire" (from the older "noumpere")
explanation: "A noumpere" was heard as "an oumpere," so "umpire" lost its first "n" exactly as "apron" and "adder" did. "Newt" went the opposite way - "an ewt" became "a newt" - and "oven" and "apple" were never reshaped like this.

steps.stem: In a book on raising children it was written: "When a child misbehaves, some parents ask first why the child acted as they did, while others ask first how the behavior can be stopped. In the end, naturally, the former also look for a way to stop the behavior, and the latter also want to know what lay behind it; what separates the two groups is only which question they put first." Which of the following statements best expresses the central claim of the text?
choices: Both groups of parents consider the same two questions, but give priority to different ones
Some parents try to understand their children's behavior, whereas others do not
Some parents react out of curiosity, whereas others react out of a wish for quiet
A parent can either understand a child's behavior or stop it, but not both
explanation: The text says outright that both groups ask both questions and differ only in order. (2) and (3) turn a difference of order into a difference of kind, and (4) invents a conflict.

steps.stem: Grammarians divide sentences into three kinds according to their purpose. A declarative sentence states something: "The shop is closed." An interrogative sentence asks something: "Is the shop closed?" An imperative sentence tells or asks the listener to do something: "Close the shop." Which of the following is an imperative sentence?
choices: The guests left the hall before midnight
Turn off the lights when you leave the hall
Who left the lights on in the hall?
Everyone in the hall stood up at once
explanation: Only (2) tells the listener to do something. (1) and (4) state facts, and (3) asks a question.

steps.stem: In Varesh, an invented language used in a fantasy novel, tense markers are attached to the end of a verb. Thus "kali" means "to eat," "kalira" means "ate," "kalisu" means "will eat" and "kalimo" means "is eating." Likewise, "petasu" means "will sleep." Therefore, which of the following words is best suited to be the Varesh word for "slept"?
choices: petara
petamo
peta
petasura
explanation: The stem for "sleep" is "peta" (from "petasu"), and the past marker is "-ra" (from "kalira"). (2) means "is sleeping," (3) is the bare verb, and (4) adds two markers.

steps.stem: Dana sent Amir a message: "At lunch I will show you the drawings that Gal made on Monday." Amir answered: "But you already told me that today I would get to see what Gal has been drawing this week." To clear up the misunderstanding, Dana underlined one word in her message and sent it back. Which of the following words is least likely to be the one Dana underlined?
choices: lunch
made
I
Monday
explanation: Amir's version blurs the time of the showing ("today"), the time of the drawing ("this week") and whether the drawings are finished ("has been drawing"). Nothing in it concerns who will do the showing, so "I" is the least likely.

steps.stem: In linguistics, two words of different meaning that differ from each other in a single sound only - such as "pin" and "bin" - are called a "minimal pair." The existence of such a pair in a language shows that the two sounds that distinguish its words are separate sounds in that language, and not merely two ways of pronouncing the same sound. In which of the following sentences do the two words in capital letters prove that "f" and "v" are separate sounds in English?
choices: His BEST shirt was hidden under a thick wool VEST he had bought in the market
The new PHASE of the project did not seem to FAZE the engineers in the least
The VOTE on the budget was held inside the old FORT at the edge of town
The FAN in the back of the delivery VAN stopped working halfway through the trip
explanation: "Fan" and "van" differ only in f/v. (1) is a minimal pair for b/v, not f/v; the words in (2) sound the same; the words in (3) differ in more than one sound.

steps.stem: At a press conference, a journalist said to the mayor: "Answer yes or no: ____" The mayor's spokesperson said: "The mayor will not answer this question, since a mayor who has done nothing wrong cannot answer it either way without lying." Which of the following questions is not suited to complete the journalist's words?
choices: Could the city's budget deficit have been caused by your decisions?
Have you stopped handing out city contracts to your friends?
Did your deputy know that you were hiding the audit report?
Were you paid well for approving the illegal building permits?
explanation: (2), (3) and (4) take the wrongdoing for granted, so both "yes" and "no" admit it. (1) asks only about a possibility, and an honest mayor can answer it truthfully.

steps.stem: This year sea turtles laid their eggs on the local beaches later than usual. A marine biologist argues that it is not reasonable to suppose that the reason is the cold winter, since a large supply of jellyfish causes the turtles to nest early. On which of the following assumptions does the biologist's argument rest?
choices: In cold winters the turtles find it hard to find jellyfish
In warm winters the turtles nest late
A cold winter brings about a large supply of jellyfish
Last winter was warmer than usual
explanation: The argument works only if a cold winter → many jellyfish → early nesting, which clashes with the late nesting; the first link is unstated. (1) would actually support the cold-winter explanation; (2) and (4) are not needed.

steps.stem: A veteran newspaper editor said: "Give me a whole page and I will write it tonight; give me half a page and I need two days; give me a single line and I need a week." Which of the following claims best expresses the editor's meaning?
choices: Short texts are better than long ones
It is harder to express an idea briefly than to write about it at length
Writers who prepare less produce better work
The importance of an article cannot be judged by its length
explanation: The shorter the text, the longer the preparation: brevity is the hard part. The other claims are not what the joke says.

steps.stem: In a column, Professor Galor wrote: "I share Professor Weiss's view that students should choose their own reading lists, but his arguments do not persuade me. In my view, the only argument for this is that choosing what to read teaches young people to judge for themselves." Which of the following could be one of Professor Weiss's arguments?
choices: When students choose their own books, they gradually learn to form opinions of their own about what is worth reading
Students who chose their own books read far fewer classic works than students whose reading lists were set by their teachers
Experienced teachers know better than their students which books will develop independent judgment in young readers
Students who choose their own books tend to go on reading many more books in the years after they finish school
explanation: Weiss's arguments must support the view and differ from Galor's; (4) offers a practical benefit. (1) is Galor's own argument in other words, and (2) and (3) argue against giving students the choice.

steps.stem: Below is a sentence from which a part (a word or a few words) is missing: "____ the heavy rain that fell throughout the night, the marathon started on time." In which of the following sentences could the missing part be the same as in the sentence above?
choices: The planning committee approved the new building plan ____ it had been presented to its members only a day earlier
The new bridge over the river was opened to the public ____ to reduce the heavy traffic in the town center
____ the objections of several residents of the neighborhood, the city council decided to widen the main road
____ of the students in the advanced class passed the final exam on their first attempt, as their teacher had expected
explanation: "Despite" (or "in spite of") fills both. In (1) the gap needs a word such as "although" before a full clause, in (2) something like "in order," and in (4) a word of quantity.

steps.stem:
Yuval: "My uncle told me that yesterday he saw Orit again, rowing on the lake with the university team, and that she looked very happy."
Neta: "____"
Neta's reply shows that Yuval's sentence can be understood in two ways, and that she understood it differently from the way he meant it. Which of the following is Neta's reply?
choices: "Your uncle was out rowing on the lake yesterday, in that cold wind?"
"And where did he see her this time?"
"And was your uncle happy to see her?"
"Does your uncle also like rowing?"
explanation: "Rowing on the lake" can describe Orit or the uncle; Neta took it to describe the uncle and put him on the lake. In (2), (3) and (4) the uncle stays where Yuval put him - on shore, with Orit doing the rowing.

steps.stem: The saying "Rest when you are tired" stands at the center of a book by a sleep researcher. The first three chapters of the book deal with questions that arise from the saying: the first asks what real rest is, as opposed to mere idleness; the second asks how a person can tell that they are tired; and the third asks whether rest should wait until tiredness sets in or should come before it. The title of each of the three chapters is the saying itself, but each time a different part of it is emphasized. Which of the following is not suited to be the title of one of the three chapters?
choices: Rest WHEN you are tired
REST when you are tired
Rest when you are TIRED
Rest when YOU are tired
explanation: The emphasized "you" answers none of the three questions. (2) matches what rest is, (3) how to tell one is tired, and (1) whether rest should wait for tiredness.

steps.stem: A composer wrote: "Written notes exist for the sake of the music, as scaffolding exists for the sake of the building: once the building stands, the scaffolding can be taken down." Which of the following statements best expresses what the composer meant?
choices: Written notes and the music they record are two separate things
Written notes are nothing more than a means of producing music
People are able to understand music only because there are written notes that record it
When a piece of music is no longer performed by musicians, its written notes are bound to be lost
explanation: Scaffolding serves the building and is then discarded; notes likewise only serve the music. (1) states a separation the image does not stress, (3) makes notes a condition of understanding, and (4) is about something else entirely.

steps.stem: A theater director said: "Actors perform differently when they know that a critic is sitting in the audience, and critics watch differently when they know that they will have to write about the actors." Which of the following best expresses the director's statement?
choices: The knowledge that a critic will review a performance affects both the actors and the critic
After a performance has been reviewed, both the acting and the criticism change
The fact that actors and critics will both be reviewed in the future affects them in the present
Actors' knowledge that they will be reviewed changes their acting, and this changes the way critics watch
explanation: One expected review affects both sides. (2) moves the effect to after the review, (3) has both sides being reviewed, and (4) invents a chain in which the actors' change causes the critics'.

steps.stem: The following appeared in an essay: "I once had no doubt that a university writing program gives a young writer something that cannot be obtained anywhere else; today I am far less sure that what writers gain from its courses exceeds what they could gain from a serious apprenticeship to an experienced author." Which of the following most accurately expresses the content of the excerpt?
choices: In the past, the author did not doubt that what is special about university writing programs is the apprenticeship to experienced authors that they offer
The author believes that today, an apprenticeship to an experienced author may benefit a young writer more than a university writing program
The author is less convinced than before that, for a young writer, the value of a university writing program is greater than that of a serious apprenticeship to an experienced author
In the past, the author was always convinced that the value of a university writing program is no greater than that of an apprenticeship
explanation: The author now doubts that the program is worth more than apprenticeship. (2) turns doubt into a preference, (1) mixes the two things being compared, and (4) reverses the author's past view.

steps.stem: Professor Adler: "Had old recordings of Kelani folk songs, made by the villagers themselves and not by folklorists, not come to light recently, I would have hesitated to back those who share Professor Ofir's view about who recorded the Kelani songs." Which of the following is not implied by Professor Adler's words?
choices: Professors Adler and Ofir now hold similar views about the recordings of the Kelani songs
Until recently, Professor Adler had doubts about Professor Ofir's view of who recorded the Kelani songs
Professor Ofir claimed that folklorists were not the only people who recorded the Kelani songs
Recordings of Kelani songs made by folklorists came to light recently
explanation: What came to light were recordings made by the villagers, not by folklorists. The rest follows: the new recordings back Ofir's view that others recorded too (3), which Adler now supports (1) after having doubted it (2).

steps.stem: Whoever announces to a group of tourists that the city museum is closed today conveys two things at once: that the museum is closed today, and that they themselves think so. So if someone makes this announcement knowing perfectly well that the museum is open, the listeners are misled on two counts - although only one falsehood was stated, since the speaker never actually said that they thought the museum was closed. Which of the following is implied in the text?
choices: A person who announces that the museum is closed today while knowing that it is open states two falsehoods
A person who says something that they themselves believe to be true cannot mislead the listener
A person who says something they believe to be true, although it is false, misleads the listener on one count only
A person who announces that the museum is closed while believing this to be false misleads the listener on two counts even if the museum really is closed without their knowing it
explanation: A sincere but mistaken speaker conveys a false fact and a true belief - one count. (1) contradicts "only one falsehood"; (2) ignores the false fact; in (4) the fact is true, so only the belief misleads.
